name: Pando
overview: Pando is a purpose-driven loyalty platform that helps businesses and their customers support verified charities. Participating retailers round up each purchase and donate the difference to a cause selected by the customer. The app allows users to discover participating businesses, explore approved charities and choose where their contributions are directed—turning everyday purchases into meaningful social impact.
challenges: Pando needed to simplify a concept involving customers, retailers, charities and recurring donations without losing clarity or trust. Through user interviews, usability testing and data analysis, we identified friction within the core experience and uncovered opportunities to improve navigation, engagement and retention. The project also required a refreshed brand and interface within a very tight delivery timeline.
outcome: We redesigned the core user flows, updated the brand aesthetic and created a more intuitive UI/UX that made the platform easier to understand and use. The improved experience decreased monthly churn by 8% while increasing average session time by approximately 30 seconds to nearly three minutes—helping Pando strengthen engagement while building a clearer foundation for growth.

name: Beaver Creek Vineyard
overview: Beaver Creek Vineyard is a family-owned winery and wedding venue in Lawrencetown, Nova Scotia. The brand refresh connects its Annapolis Valley roots with a clean, rustic visual identity that reflects the warmth of the family and the surrounding landscape.
challenges: New ownership called for a fresh identity that respected the vineyard’s history. The challenge was to create a bold, distinctly Canadian logo and an authentic, organic visual style that felt familiar to locals while welcoming a new generation of guests.
outcome: The refreshed brand captured the vineyard’s character and the appeal of its weddings and events. Local visitors responded with enthusiasm and support, recognising an identity that felt connected to the place, its community and the experience it offers.

name: Collab.
tagline: Stay in the moment. Relive the memory, together.
overview: Collab is a media-sharing startup backed by more than $2.5 million in funding. Built for weddings, sports, concerts and conferences, the app makes it easy to collect moments in shared albums across devices and operating systems, bringing everyone’s perspective together.
challenges: When I joined, the team needed clearer product direction and discipline. I focused on defining the ideal customer, unique value proposition, core user journey and North Star metrics, giving the team a shared framework for prioritising features and evaluating progress.
outcome: Stitch combined participants’ photos and music into one event highlight after a shared countdown. The product generated approximately $1,000 in monthly recurring revenue, achieved 21% stickiness (daily active users divided by monthly active users) and converted 26% of free users to paid.

name: Advanced Medical Pods
overview: Advanced Medical Pods (AMP) is a remote healthcare prototype developed for the Canadian Space Agency’s Health Beyond initiative. My work connected product design, patient and clinician experiences, and brand identity to support access to care in medically isolated communities.
challenges: A tight timeline demanded clear priorities across a complex, connected system. The experience needed to bring TEMI’s AI-assisted initial triage, connected medical devices and remote consultations into an understandable patient journey, with a consistent identity across every touchpoint.
outcome: The design work brought patient and clinician software, connected-device interactions and a complete brand identity into one cohesive prototype experience. A shared visual language carried across interfaces and physical applications, making the ambitious remote care concept easier to understand.

name: Bar Kismet
tagline: A personal touch. A lasting impression.
overview: Bar Kismet is an award-winning seafood restaurant and cocktail bar in Halifax, Nova Scotia, founded by my brother Jenner Cormier and his wife, Annie Brace-Lavoie. With their creative direction, I helped shape a brand rooted in family, craft and hospitality.
challenges: The challenge was preserving the character of our grandmother Maureen Tufts’s handwriting while scanning and retracing it into a distinctive logo. Earthy colours and vintage details needed to balance simplicity with ornament, creating an identity that felt refined and approachable.
outcome: The identity centres on Maureen’s handwriting, honouring her love of cooking and ingredients prepared by hand. An earthy palette and subtle ornament bring Jenner and Annie’s vision together: personal, organic and quietly elegant, with the warmth of a family story.

name: IMSI
overview: IMSI develops monitoring and measurement technology for the steel industry. I refreshed its brand applications and marketing materials while retaining the established logo, alongside a website design focused on clearer user journeys and more accessible communication of its technical offering.
challenges: The challenge was introducing a fresh visual approach without losing the recognition of IMSI’s existing brand. The website also needed clearer priorities: identifying core user journeys and translating those findings into UX flows that helped visitors navigate complex technical information.
outcome: The work delivered refreshed marketing materials and a website design built around the identified user journeys. The existing logo anchored a more cohesive visual approach. Website implementation and hosting were handled externally; this case study presents my original design work.

name: Starling Architects
tagline: An evolving practice. A connected identity.
overview: Starling Architects, an architecture firm in Halifax, Nova Scotia, commissioned brand refresh concepts to explore its next chapter. My work included an evolved logo, a brand playbook and marketing materials showing how a more connected identity could reflect the practice’s growth.
challenges: The firm’s conservative early branding offered limited room to communicate its value and reach potential clients through organic search. The challenge was evolving the existing logo into a more mature identity while giving every application a clearer, more consistent voice.
outcome: The concepts presented a cohesive direction across the logo, playbook and marketing materials, showing how the brand could grow while retaining its identity. This exploratory work gave Starling a tangible view of a more mature, consistent presence across future applications.

name: Urbanarc Real Estate Group
overview: Urbanarc Real Estate Group needed a new brand to appeal to buyers seeking contemporary, upscale homes. I developed a logo, brand guide and reusable visual assets, establishing a clean, modern identity that could carry consistently across property marketing and communications.
challenges: The logo needed to express the Urbanarc name through a symbol inspired by Noah’s ark, paired with a clean, contemporary typeface. The challenge was balancing that distinctive reference with an upscale feel and the clarity needed across varied marketing applications.
outcome: The identity pairs an ark-inspired symbol with modern typography and a consistent visual language. A brand guide and supporting assets provide a practical foundation for future design work, helping Urbanarc present a cohesive presence across property promotions and branded materials.

name: Anapolie Pizza
tagline: A family tradition. A fresh look.
overview: Family owned since 1983, Anapolie Pizza is a community staple in Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia, known for quality pizza and welcoming service. Working with a close friend, I refreshed the brand and supported website updates while honouring the shop’s history.
challenges: The refresh needed to preserve the familiarity customers valued while giving the brand renewed character. Logo variations had to suit different applications, including a version featuring a likeness of founder Joseph Chidiac, without losing a consistent connection to Anapolie’s identity.
outcome: The work produced a flexible family of logos, including a character inspired by Joseph Chidiac, who founded Anapolie in 1983. Together with website support, the refresh gave the shop a renewed visual identity grounded in its family and community roots.
